rule: A verification gate may not assert a function or constant it itself defines. Entries below are PRE-EXISTING violations, frozen so the class cannot grow. NEW violations fail the gate. Entries that stop violating are reported STALE and must be removed (run --write-baseline) so the list cannot rot upward. An entry carrying `retained_because` is a DELIBERATE, argued exception rather than unpaid debt; an entry carrying `diagnosis` is unpaid debt whose cause has been measured but not yet fixed. Both fields are preserved across re-baselines.

violations.retained_because: DETECTOR OVER-MATCH ON DERIVED DATA, reviewed 260729. Every subject this gate asserts resolves OUTSIDE it: it reads six real files (connector-registry.ts, routes/sources.ts, cockpit-chat.ts, lib/observability.ts, and two governance YAMLs) and asserts 3-way id-set equality between code and manifest. The symbols the detector names are (i) `setEq`, a pure two-argument comparison utility, and (ii) `codeIds`/`yamlIds`/`manifestFields`/`codeKinds`/`manifestKinds`, each of which is `const x = [...someFile.matchAll(...)].map(...)`. The detector classifies a `const` bound to a token starting with `[` as a FIXTURE (const-array literal); a spread-of-a-call is derived data, not a fixture. Clearing this entry would mean rewriting `[...m.matchAll()]` as `Array.from(m.matchAll())` so the detector reclassifies it — a cosmetic dodge that changes no behaviour. Kept rather than gamed. If the detector is ever taught to distinguish `[...call()]` from `[literal, literal]`, this entry should go STALE on its own.
violations.known_gap: This gate has no --self-test at all. That is a real, separate weakness; it is not what the P-2 entry is about.

violations.retained_because: EXPECTATION LISTS, NOT FIXTURES, reviewed 260729. Each of the seven `gate(...)` closures reads a REAL artifact (migrations 009/010/011 SQL, dal/types.ts, dal/types/inference.ts, DalAdapter.ts, WorkersDalAdapter.ts) and checks it against a hard-coded list of required markers — `required`, `alterCols`, `signals`, `thresholds`, `stubMethods`. Those arrays are the CONTRACT the migration must satisfy, not a fixture the gate then asserts about itself; the subject under test is the file on disk. The available clear is to move the marker lists into an external JSON contract so the detector sees `const required = JSON.parse(read(...))`. That is a genuine improvement (the expectation becomes reviewable and diffable outside the gate) and is the recommended follow-up, but it was not done in this pass and the entry is NOT being cleared by relabelling.
violations.known_gap: No --self-test, and the assertions are string-greps over SQL/TS text, which is the weakest gate class in the estate. Both are real; neither is the P-2 violation.

violations.diagnosis: UNPAID DEBT — cause measured 260729, fix NOT applied. The single self-referential callsite is in the --self-test: `validateEntryContracts(staleAgent, staleClaude)` where `validateEntryContracts` is defined in this file and both fixtures are string literals defined in this file. It proves a function returns the strings it was written to return; it never runs this gate as a process and never observes an exit code. The fix is the same shape applied to verify-tenant-source-isolation / verify-domain-scaffold-honest-empty / verify-flag-parse-hygiene in this pass: add a `--root=` override, have the self-test write AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md carrying the stale shadow-only claims (plus a minimal src/workers so only the intended detector fires) into a temp root, SPAWN this gate at it, and assert exit 1; control = the real repo root at exit 0.

UNPAID DEBT — cause measured 260729, fix NOT applied. The flagged callsite is `emit('verify-customer-ecosystem-template', failures, { required_files: required.length })`; `required` is a 16-entry const-array literal of required template paths. Strictly this is a METRIC in the emit payload rather than an assertion subject — the asserted subject is `failures` — so the detector is partly over-matching here. The honest clear is nevertheless available and worth doing: move the 16-path required list into an external contract (e.g. docs/contracts/CUSTOMER_ECOSYSTEM_TEMPLATE_CONTRACT.json) so the template's contract is reviewable outside the gate and the gate reads it, add a `--template-root=` override, add a denominator guard (a contract listing zero required files must exit 2, not pass vacuously), and add a --self-test that spawns this gate against a temp template root with one required file deleted and observes exit 1. This gate currently has NO self-test and is the only baseline entry with external_subject=false.
